one_month_reasoning: No Jabil earnings fall before 2026-11-01 (Q1 FY27 is mid-December against a $3.80-4.20 core EPS guide). The 2026-09-30 print already happened: -10.0% close to close (318.84 to 286.86) on a ~3.7% beat of the $16.92 consensus, then +6% over two sessions to 304.41. In the window: Celestica Q3 on 2026-10-26, Flex Q2 FY27 in late October, hyperscaler Q3 calls (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta) with 2027 capex commentary, and the FY26 10-K. Chain evidence points to 2027 capex still growing (~+25-29% per UBS/Morgan Stanley consensus) with deceleration in 2028, so the late-October calls are more likely to confirm 2027 than to shock it, but the July-2026 drawdown shows the group reacts violently to any hint of digestion. I see no reliable directional edge, so I keep a near-symmetric spread at ~13.6% monthly vol (47%/3.46), median ~305, with slightly fat tails for the capex-call event risk. Unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (FY28 core EPS ~$20.5 x 16x = $328, 60%) and FCF yield (FY28 adj FCF ~$1.8B / ~100M diluted shares = $18.0 at 5.5% = $327, 40%) = ~$327 twelve months out.

inputs_detail.derivation: Corrected from round 1's +50% per supervisor check of the call.

FY27 $17.55 grown ~17%: low-teens revenue growth (chain consensus has 2027 hyperscaler capex +25-29%, with 2028 decelerating to ~6% per UBS, so Jabil's FY28 cloud growth slows sharply), ~20bp margin from absorbing the 4M sq ft ramp, ~3% buyback shrink. Jabil's +13%/+19% beats vs initial guide in FY25/FY26 are a cushion I do not add to the base.

Flex ~25x its raised FY27 guide and Celestica ~34x current-year are richer, but JBL deserves a discount: lower margin, payables-funded working capital (+$8B in FY26, AP $14.4B vs equity $1.6B per the 8-K), and GAAP EPS 26% below core. At the horizon the market will be looking at 2028 capex growth near single digits (UBS), which argues against a re-rating. 16x vs 17.3x today.

bear.story: 2027 hyperscaler capex flattens instead of growing ~25%, or a top customer pauses/consigns a rack program (as in FY24, when cloud revenue fell on a shift to consignment). Sensitivity: a flat-capex year leaves Jabil's FY27 cloud line short of $17.5B and FY28 cloud flat-to-down ~15% (~-$2.6B revenue at ~8-10% incremental operating margin = ~$2/share), putting FY28 core EPS near $17.5-18; with payables normalising and the multiple back at a pre-AI ~11x, ~$195.

base.story: Jabil delivers roughly the $44.5B / $17.55 FY27 guide (perhaps a modest beat, as in FY25/FY26); 2027 capex grows ~25% as consensus expects; the late-September 2027 Q4 print guides FY28 core EPS ~$20-21, but with 2028 capex growth decelerating the multiple settles ~16x.

bull.story: 2027 capex lands at the high end ($1.2-1.4T per Morgan Stanley/Goldman), Vera Rubin and ASIC rack ramps push cloud well above $17.5B, another big beat vs guide (FY26 was +19%), FY28 EPS ~$23 and a re-rating toward 20x, still below Flex.

thesis_break_reason: ~$205 is ~11.7x the $17.55 FY27 guide and equals my flat-2027-capex case (FY28 EPS ~$17.5 at ~11-12x): a close there would mean the market is pricing a guide cut from a hyperscaler pause, a program loss or consignment shift, or a payables/working-capital unwind, not ordinary 47%-vol noise. It sits well below the ~$284-287 lows that held through the July-Sept 2026 AI-hardware selloff and the post-print drop.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor confirmed my peer multiples and the FY27 guide, corrected AI revenue to +54% ($22.1B) with networking only +15%, and asked me to weigh working capital and quantify a flat-capex year. Follow-up chain research: UBS (Reuters, July 2026) models hyperscaler capex +76% in 2026, +25% in 2027 and +6% in 2028; Morgan Stanley/consensus put 2027 cloud capex up ~29%; Sanmina reiterated >$16B FY27 revenue on AI racks; Celestica reports 2026-10-26. So 2027 still looks like a growth year for the chain, but by October 2027 the market will be pricing a sharp 2028 slowdown, which caps the exit multiple. Jabil's own FY24 history (cloud revenue down on a consignment shift) shows how quickly a single hyperscaler decision can move the cloud line. Valuation: FY28 core EPS $20.5 x 16x = $328; FCF $1.8B / 100M shares (raised from 98M) at 5.5% = $327; blend $327, about 7% above spot. The working-capital point (+$8B payables, GAAP EPS 26% below core) is why I stay at 16x/5.5% rather than moving toward Flex's ~25x; I do not cut further because the guide-beat record (+13%, +19%) offsets it. Scenarios 195/330/470 at 25/53/22 give a mean ~$327. Mapped to a lognormal-ish distribution with median ~$320 and sigma ~0.42 with a fattened left tail: P(>=304) 0.55, P(>=411) 0.265, P(>=213) 0.83. Upper tail trimmed slightly from round 1 for the 2028-deceleration risk at the horizon. The Manifold market (resolved N/A) was dropped as a source. Some trade sources (TVBS/Taipei Times, TrendForce summary, TechWire Asia) remain second-hand and are used only directionally.
